skill.name: style-audit
skill.description: Audits code against CI/CD style rules, quality guidelines, and best practices, then rewrites code to meet standards without breaking functionality. Use this skill after functionality validation to ensure code is not just correct but also maintainable, readable, and production-ready. The skill applies linting rules, enforces naming conventions, improves code organization, and refactors for clarity while preserving all behavioral correctness verified by functionality audits.
skill.summary: Audits working code for style, maintainability, documentation, and CI readiness.
skill.author: DNYoussef

content.value_statement: Teams need code that is correct, readable, maintainable, and aligned with project standards. This skill guides style review, safe refactoring, documentation checks, and quality reporting after functionality is validated.
actual_capabilities: Runs language-appropriate linting and formatting checks when tools are available.
Reviews naming, decomposition, complexity, documentation, error handling, security, and performance.
Prioritizes style issues by risk, readability, maintainability, and user impact.
Applies automated formatting fixes before manual refactoring when appropriate.
Rewrites code for clarity while preserving verified behavior through tests.
Produces reports with findings, refactoring notes, remaining issues, and quality metrics.
limitations: It depends on available linters, test suites, and project configuration.
It should run after functionality validation, not replace it.
It may need team guidance when multiple style choices are valid.
It cannot prove security or performance without relevant tests and runtime evidence.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Improve naming, formatting, documentation, and error handling before asking teammates for review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Inherited Code
use_cases.description: Audit working code against team conventions and create a prioritized cleanup plan.

use_cases.title: Enforce CI Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Align linting, formatting, type checks, and security review with CI expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Review Style Issues
prompt_templates.scenario: First pass on a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the selected files for style, readability, naming, and documentation issues. Report findings before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Safe Formatting Problems
prompt_templates.prompt: Run available linting and formatting checks on this project. Apply safe automated fixes, then summarize what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor for Maintainability
prompt_templates.prompt: After confirming tests pass, refactor complex functions for clarity. Preserve behavior and explain the tests that support each change.

prompt_templates.title: Create a CI Style Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the codebase against our style goals and CI checks. Propose phased fixes, tool configuration changes, and remaining risks.

output_examples.input: Audit a JavaScript feature branch before review.
output: Found inconsistent naming, missing error handling, and two long functions.
Applied formatting fixes and proposed a smaller refactor for the complex functions.
Recommended adding a regression test before changing validation logic.

output_examples.input: Review Python service code after functionality tests pass.
output_examples.output: The audit reports linting issues, missing type hints, weak docstrings, and one inefficient loop. It suggests ordered fixes and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Create a style report for a team handoff.
output: Summarized overall code quality and the highest-impact style risks.
Grouped findings by formatting, naming, complexity, documentation, and error handling.
Listed deferred issues with effort estimates and recommended priority.

best_practices: Run functionality tests before and after each significant style change.
Provide team style guidelines and lint configurations before the audit.
Separate automated formatting, manual refactoring, and documentation updates into reviewable changes.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to change untested behavior during a style cleanup.
Treating default linter settings as team standards without review.
Applying large refactors without explaining risk, tests, and remaining issues.

faq.question: Does this skill replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It removes style noise and prepares clearer code, but human review should still evaluate design and intent.

faq.question: Can it edit code directly?
faq.answer: Yes, when asked. It prioritizes safe automated fixes and should verify behavior with tests.

faq.question: Which languages does it support?
faq.answer: It is language-agnostic. It recommends common tools such as ESLint, Prettier, Black, flake8, pylint, and mypy when relevant.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after functionality is validated and before pull requests, handoff, or CI quality gate work.

faq.question: Will it enforce my team style guide?
faq.answer: Yes, if you provide the guide or configuration. Without it, the skill uses general maintainability practices.

faq.question: Can it find security issues?
faq.answer: It includes secure coding review for input validation, sensitive data handling, and common attack surfaces. It is not a full penetration test.
